title: Payment step 2 — the one call that moves value across the border
description: max_amount_in is set 1% above the quoted amount_in as a slippage ceiling. The response is an acknowledgement, not a settlement: status is BRIDGE_IN_PROGRESS and a swap_id comes back to poll.
notes: Gateway: Banco de San Jose commercial-bank gateway, spoke-crc. COOKIE ONLY — this endpoint is RequireCookieAuth, not RequireAnyAuth; a bearer token will not work here even though it does on the bridge and liquidity routes. Requires the commercial_bank realm role; the platform's shared 403 text claiming 'requires CENTRAL_BANK role' is wrong for this operation. payer_bank_id is deprecated and ignored — identity comes from the session. THE WHOLE max_amount_in IS BRIDGED IN before the AMM executes, because the realised input is unknown until execution; the unspent remainder comes back as a separate RESIDUE bridge position. Behind this single POST, four relay-only steps run on two Central Bank gateways: bridge-in and the Hub swap signed by the payer's issuing CB, bridge-out by the BENEFICIARY's CB (CB-A burning CB-B's tokens would be a sovereignty breach), then residue return. That is why one POST produces asynchronous multi-Central-Bank state, and why BRIDGE_OUT_FAILED is expressible: the swap succeeded and delivery did not. Undocumented upstream: 422 with error_code in TRANSFER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, POOL_NOT_ACTIVE, CIRCUIT_BREAKER_HALTED, BRIDGE_IN_FAILED, SWAP_FAILED.
